verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four cases have outcome dates that precede the fitting date: case One was 'fitted 4 May' but the extra 340 hours are measured 'by 27 March', and case Three was 'fitted 2 August' but measured 'by 21 July'. The reported gain in those cases is dated before the redesigned bearing was installed.

Rainfall is an alternative cause that fits all four plots and demonstrably reaches them: 'Rainfall in each plot's season ran a fifth higher than the year before' while 'every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule', so the extra water was not offset. Since each plot is compared against the previous summer, the 8-13 cm gain is equally explained by the wetter season rather than the fertilizer.

Two of the four cohorts are measured before the email was sent: cohort One was 'emailed 24 March' but retention is read 'by 9 March', and cohort Three was 'emailed 25 October' but read 'by 10 October'. Those retention lifts predate the intervention they are attributed to.

The timings cover a narrower population than the claim: 'Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route', so roughly 17 percent of runs -- precisely the ones most likely to have gone wrong or run long -- are excluded from the 5-9 minute improvement. Separately, 'Order volume through each depot hit a record low, half the earlier period', which is an unaddressed depot-level difference from the comparison month.
